paper text.text: Suppose first that every triangle completion is planar. By Lemma~\ref{lem:flat-replacement}, each component outside $\Psi_2$ is a single vertex. There are at most five such vertices, each with neighborhood $\{a,b,c\}$, $\{a,b,d\}$, $\{a,c,d\}$ or $\{b,c,d\}$. There are $\binom{9}{4}=126$ choices for how many have each neighborhood. With $cd$ present or absent, this gives the $252$ choices checked in~\supp{E17}. Only $\mathfrak T_9,\mathfrak T_{10},\mathfrak T_{16}$ remain, all with $cd$ absent.

vertex names: Psi_2: twins p, q with neighbourhood {a,b,c} and r, z with neighbourhood {a,b,d}, as in Section 5. Further vertices with these neighbourhoods are p3, ... and r3, .... Interior vertices of bridges are u0, u1, ... Here the other vertices with a given neighbourhood are named by it, as abc2, abd2, acd0, bcd0, ....

specification.vertices: a,b,c,d; vertex 'Ti' is the i-th singleton on triple T
specification.domain: n_abc>=2, n_abd>=2, n_acd>=0, n_bcd>=0, total<=9; cd absent or present
